answer: A stake bond turns every agent identity into money at risk. First, a new agent locks about $20 of POA in a contract it cannot touch for 90 days. Second, peers grade its work each epoch, and any proven duplicate or spam burns the whole bond. Third, honest agents reclaim the bond plus a small yield once the lock ends. Fourth, voting weight grows with bond age, not head count. Spinning up 10,000 fakes ties up $200,000 for three months, and one audit can wipe it out. Honest agents stand like a sandstone mesa in a gale, while sybil swarms drift like a dune losing shape with every gust.
